text: Key reproductive terms in pigs: abortion (delivery of a premature, non-viable litter less than 111 days after mating); agalactia (shortage or absence of milk); cryptorchid (a male whose testicles have not descended into the scrotum and remain in the abdomen or inguinal canal, unable to produce fertile sperm); embryo (the developing offspring up to day 30 after fertilization, after which it is called a fetus); endometritis (infection of the uterus); fetus (from 30 days to delivery); mastitis (inflammation associated with infection of the mammary gland); MMA — Mastitis Metritis Agalactia (no milk or colostrum at delivery, with fever, loss of appetite, and a painful udder, usually caused by E. coli); mummified piglet (a piglet that died in the uterus during pregnancy, with tissue and fluid reabsorbed, leaving skin and skeleton); oestrus (the 2–3 day period during which the sow accepts the boar; the oestrus cycle — time from one oestrus to the next — is usually 19–22 days); orchitis (inflammation of the testicle, usually from Japanese encephalitis or Brucellosis); oxytocin (hormone from the sow causing uterine contractions and milk release, which can also be injected to stimulate these functions); prostaglandins (hormone inducing cervix opening and contraction); repeat breeding (estrus reappearing after mating or AI when the embryo fails to develop properly); stillborn piglet (a piglet that dies during delivery); weaning (separation of piglets from the sow after suckling, usually at 21–28 days).
